messages:
elaine: quick follow-up from the svc-auth RFC — thinking about a lightweight pattern we called 'shadow lease proxy' for service-to-service when callers are libs or external integrators. wanted to capture tradeoffs and a small migration plan.

matt: example pls? not sure what "shadow lease" means here.

elaine: short: instead of issuing long-lived API keys to integrators, we mint very short-lived "lease tokens" via a proxy service that holds the long-lived credential. callers get a lease (10m) scoped to the req. proxy enforces rate/role and emits audit events. shadow = integrator never sees the long-lived secret.

zach: ok that matches what i pictured. pros: no long-lived secrets in client env, easier rotation. cons: increased ops surface + latency.

raj: latency concern is real — but we can cache leases per caller+scope for 30s and use jittered refresh. also keep fallback to dedicated API key for high-throughput partners.

elaine: good point. thoughts on scoping semantics? two options: per-project lease vs per-org lease. project-scoped leases are more restrictive but require more lookups. org-scoped simpler for multi-project partners.

matt: prefer project-scoped by default, allow org-scoped on approval. enforcement: proxy checks caller identity -> allowed project list.

zach: how do we model RBAC? lease should carry minimal claims: issuer, subject, scope (read/write), allowed-projects[], exp. Example token payload: ```{
  "iss": "lease-proxy.redwood-internal",
  "sub": "partner:acme-inc:svc-a",
  "scope": "generate:models",
  "projects": ["proj-123", "proj-456"],
  "exp": 1718235167
}```

raj: +1. Token format OK. We need to ensure runtime checks use both token claims and resource-level ACLs (double-check).

elaine: audit/telemetry: proxy must log minted-lease -> original API key id, caller identity, scope, TTL. that lets us trace back to who requested. security-bot: "alert:lease-minted" will fire on high-risk scopes.

matt: migration plan idea: 1) implement proxy in beta; 2) support wrappers in our SDKs (node/py) that exchange long-lived key for lease transparently; 3) invite 2 partners for opt-in; 4) require for all new external keys after 90d.

zach: SDK wrappers should expose a simple method: `withLease(key, scope, fn)` that refreshes when near-expiry. keep fallback when proxy unavailable.

elaine: ops: proxy will need quotas and circuit-breakers. also plan for emergency bypass where a support engineer can mint a longer (1h) lease with justification. all bypass actions logged and require 2 approvals.

raj: rotation story: underlying long-lived keys can be rotated without rotating leases. good. but we need to avoid silent permission creep — periodic re-eval of allowed-projects on lease refresh.

matt: compatibility: for partners that cannot adopt SDK, provide a simple sidecar container that handles exchange locally. doc + docker image.

zach: what about service-auth between our internal services (not partners)? do we use same proxy? probably not — internal services can use mTLS or ephemeral certs. keep separation.

elaine: agreed. plan = partner-facing proxy only. internal mesh continues with existing ephemeral tokens.

security-bot: ACTIONS: create RFC addendum for shadow-lease proxy; implement minimal lease schema + audit events; design SDK wrappers; shortlist 2 pilot partners.

elaine: i'll draft the addendum and share a short design doc. tagging folks: @matt @zach @raj for review. thanks all :thumbsup:
